cases.vignette: A 3-year-old has had fever for 6 days. Conjunctival injection and lip changes are present, but not all typical Kawasaki findings. Adenovirus PCR is positive, with elevated CRP, hypoalbuminemia, and sterile pyuria. The initial echocardiogram is normal.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Do a positive viral test and a normal echocardiogram exclude incomplete Kawasaki disease? What further evaluation is needed, and what are the criteria for starting treatment?

cases.title: Pediatrics - Persistent fever despite a positive adenovirus test

cases.vignette: A patient presents within 90 minutes of symptom onset with mild aphasia and impaired fine motor function of the dominant hand, yielding an NIHSS score of 2. CT shows no hemorrhage, and CTA shows no LVO. The patient is not taking anticoagulants and has no other clear contraindications.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Would you exclude reperfusion therapy solely because the score is low? How would you distinguish disabling from nondisabling deficits and incorporate that assessment into treatment selection?

cases.title: Neurology - Low NIHSS score but substantial impairment of daily function

cases.vignette: A patient with CKD receiving cefepime has a generalized seizure, followed by persistent confusion and intermittent myoclonus for at least 45 minutes. Glucose and Na are normal, and CT shows no acute lesion.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: How would you distinguish a postictal state, nonconvulsive status epilepticus, and drug-induced neurotoxicity? How would you prioritize urgent EEG, drug discontinuation, and additional antiseizure treatment?

cases.title: Neurology - The seizure has stopped, but consciousness has not returned

cases.vignette: A patient with myasthenia gravis develops dysphagia and a weak cough after a respiratory infection. SpO₂ is 97%, but FVC has declined over several hours and neck muscle strength is also worsening.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Are ICU care and securing the airway needed despite normal oxygen saturation? How would you assess respiratory mechanics, bulbar symptoms, and the clinical course?

questions.label: Follow-up Question
questions.text: How would you choose between IVIG and plasma exchange for this patient's myasthenia gravis exacerbation?

cases.title: Neurology - Myasthenia gravis exacerbation with normal SpO₂

cases.vignette: A patient taking steroids develops acute knee pain and a low-grade fever. Synovial fluid WBC is 72,000/µL, urate crystals are present, and Gram stain is negative.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Is it appropriate to diagnose gout and intensify steroid treatment? What are the limitations of crystal detection and a negative Gram stain in excluding infection, and how would you decide on cultures, antibiotics, and drainage?

cases.title: Rheumatology - Acute monoarthritis with crystals present

cases.vignette: A patient with SLE has fever, new proteinuria, hematuria, and rising creatinine. Complement is low and anti-dsDNA is elevated, but cough and pulmonary infiltrates are also present, and culture results are pending.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: How would you evaluate lupus nephritis and infection simultaneously? How would you sequence antimicrobial treatment, kidney biopsy, and intensified immunosuppression, and what are the risks of delay?

cases.title: Rheumatology - SLE flare, infection, or both?

cases.vignette: A patient is scheduled to receive rituximab for RA. HBsAg is negative, anti-HBc and anti-HBs are positive, HBV DNA is undetectable, and liver enzyme levels are normal.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Is follow-up testing alone sufficient because antibodies are present? How does HBV reactivation risk vary by drug, and is prophylactic antiviral treatment needed?

questions.label: Follow-up Question
questions.text: What is the plan for monitoring HBV reactivation after rituximab treatment ends?

cases.title: Rheumatology - HBV antibodies in a patient scheduled for rituximab

cases.vignette: A patient has fever, confusion, thrombocytopenia, and hemolytic anemia. Schistocytes are present, LDH is elevated, and creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL. PT/aPTT are nearly normal, and ADAMTS13 results will take several days.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: How would you assess the likelihood of TTP and decide whether to start treatment before confirmation? How appropriate are plasma exchange, immunotherapy, and platelet transfusion?

cases.title: Hematology and Oncology - A patient with suspected TTP and DIC

cases.vignette: On day 6 of heparin exposure, the platelet count falls from 240,000→88,000/µL. There is no new thrombosis, and surgical-site bleeding was controlled the previous day. Infection is also present, so alternative causes are possible.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: How would you integrate the 4Ts score with test results?

questions.label: Follow-up Question
questions.text: While test results are pending, how would you decide on stopping heparin, selecting an alternative anticoagulant, and tailoring anticoagulation intensity to the bleeding risk?

cases.title: Hematology and Oncology - Postoperative thrombocytopenia and bleeding risk

cases.vignette: A patient develops fever with an ANC of 180/µL after chemotherapy for a solid tumor. Blood pressure is stable and the MASCC score is in the low-risk range, but new right lower quadrant pain and diarrhea are present.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Is outpatient treatment appropriate based on the score alone? How would you evaluate for neutropenic enterocolitis and decide on imaging, hospitalization, and antimicrobial coverage?

cases.title: Hematology and Oncology - Febrile neutropenia with a low-risk score but abdominal pain

cases.vignette: A patient on long-term lithium develops confusion and dysarthria. The lithium level is 1.5 mmol/L, with mild hypercalcemia. Polyuria and rising Na subsequently develop.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Is it appropriate to attribute the neurologic symptoms to another metabolic abnormality? How would you assess chronic lithium toxicity and nephrogenic DI, and what are the criteria for repeat testing, nephrology consultation, and evaluation for extracorporeal removal?

cases.title: Psychiatry - Prominent neurologic symptoms with a slightly elevated lithium level

cases.vignette: A patient has been treated for recurrent depression. During the interview, the patient denies mania, but family members describe past periods lasting a few days with reduced sleep, excessive spending, and uncharacteristic confidence. Depression and agitation are currently present together.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: How would you evaluate unipolar depression, the bipolar spectrum, and mixed features?

questions.label: Follow-up Question
questions.text: What history and treatment considerations are needed before intensifying antidepressant monotherapy?

cases.title: Psychiatry - Recurrent depression and brief periods of increased activity

cases.vignette: An older patient with a history of heart failure develops dyspnea and hypoxemia during or immediately after a transfusion. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and elevated blood pressure are present, without a clear fever.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: What should be stopped and reported immediately? What observations help distinguish TACO, TRALI, and other transfusion reactions, and what tests and interventions would you anticipate?

cases.title: Nursing - Dyspnea immediately after transfusion

cases.vignette: A patient receiving high-dose methotrexate shows delayed decline in methotrexate levels and elevated liver enzymes after concomitant ciprofloxacin and vancomycin. Changes in kidney function also need evaluation.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: How would you review DDIs and other factors contributing to toxicity or delayed elimination?

questions.label: Follow-up Question
questions.text: Which drugs should be stopped or replaced, how should drug levels and organ function be monitored, and what are the criteria for escalating rescue treatment?

cases.title: Pharmacy - Delayed methotrexate elimination and concomitant antibiotics

cases.vignette: A patient with MRSA pneumonia develops AKI during vancomycin treatment. A switch to linezolid is being considered, but the patient has been taking sertraline long term.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Should concomitant use be ruled out categorically? What would you recommend after considering the need for antimicrobial treatment, available alternatives, the effects of stopping the antidepressant, and monitoring for serotonin toxicity?

cases.title: Pharmacy - Linezolid is needed, but the patient is taking an SSRI

cases.vignette: A kidney transplant recipient taking tacrolimus is diagnosed with early COVID-19. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is being considered, but rapid drug-level testing is difficult to obtain over the weekend.

questions.label: Question
questions.text: Does the care setting allow safe management of the interaction between nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and tacrolimus in this patient? How would you proceed with alternative antiviral treatment and consultation with the transplant team?

questions.label: Follow-up Question
questions.text: What monitoring for the tacrolimus interaction is needed even after nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment ends?

cases.title: Pharmacy - COVID-19 treatment in a patient taking tacrolimus
